source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Guaranteeing that the procedure will have a successful outcome, which is not what a witness signature on this form actually confirms","B":"That the nurse observed the client sign the authentic document, rather than personally explaining the risks and benefits as the family is currently asking about","C":"That the nurse personally explained the risks and benefits, similar to what the client's family is currently assuming this witnessing role means","D":"That the client has no right to change their mind later, which is not an accurate description of what this witnessed consent actually means"}}
source_row.rationale: The nurse's role in witnessing a signature on an informed consent form specifically confirms that the nurse observed the client sign the document and that the signature appears authentic — it does not mean the nurse personally provided or is responsible for the procedure-specific risk/benefit information, which remains the responsibility of the provider performing the procedure, though the nurse should still verify the client's general understanding and notify the provider if concerns arise.
source_row.source_detail: Scope of the Nursing Witness Role in Informed Consent

source_row.stem: A nurse witnesses a client's signature on an informed consent form for a surgical procedure, and the client's family later asks whether this witnessing means the nurse also personally explained all the risks and benefits of the procedure.
